plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden faces that tilt across the sky, ringed with bright petals around a dark, seed-packed center. Late-summer fields glow with them, and bees crowd every bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July to September)
plants.location: Great Plains and farmland across the central United States and Canada, plus much of temperate Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is made of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual florets. Each floret becomes a seed. Young buds track the sun from east to west during the day.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Moorlands and heaths turn into rolling carpets of tiny bell-shaped flowers. The purple haze reaches the horizon, hums with bees, and smells faintly of honey.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (typically August to October)
plants.location: Moors and heathlands of Scotland, northern England, and Scandinavia
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its thick, jelly-like texture. Moorland beekeepers sometimes move their hives onto the hills in August to catch the bloom.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Fluffy, perfumed golden pom-poms cover this Australian tree. Winter and early spring bring a bright burst of color to bushland, with nectar-seeking birds and insects in constant motion.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
